title: Whole genome sequence of Microbacterium lacticum strain B30 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer after cleaning and disinfection
author: Sadiq, Faizan Ahmed
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: Whole genome sequence of Microbacterium lacticum strain B30 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer following cleaning and disinfection in the FASTA format. The bacteria was grown overnight in BHI broth and its DNA was extracted using the Qiagen tissue culture DNA extraction kit (DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits). The genomic DNA was randomly sheared into short fragments. The obtained fragments were end repaired, A-tailed and further ligated with Illumina adapter. The library was checked with Qubit and real-time PCR for quantification and bioanalyzer for size distribution detection. Quantified libraries were pooled and sequenced on Illumina platform (NovaSeq

steps.title: Grow bacteria overnight
steps.instruction: Inoculate Microbacterium lacticum strain B30 into BHI broth and incubate for an overnight period.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Harvest cells and extract genomic DNA using the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (tissue culture DNA extraction kit).

steps.title: Shear DNA into fragments
steps.instruction: Randomly shear the extracted genomic DNA to generate short fragments.

steps.title: End‑repair, A‑tail and ligate adapters
steps.instruction: Perform end‑repair of the sheared fragments, add an A‑tail, and ligate Illumina adapters to the prepared ends.

steps.title: Library quality control
steps.instruction: Quantify the library with Qubit and real‑time PCR, and assess fragment size distribution using a Bioanalyzer.

steps.title: Pool and sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Pool the quantified libraries and sequence them on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, adjusting the run according to the effective library concentration and the required amount of data.

steps.title: Clean raw sequencing data
steps.instruction: Process the raw reads with the Clean Data pipeline (details not specified) to obtain high‑quality reads for assembly.

steps.title: Assemble with SOAPdenovo
steps.instruction: Run SOAPdenovo using K‑mers of 95, 107 and 119 (selected based on project type); determine the optimal K‑mer and adjust other parameters to obtain the preliminary assembly with the fewest scaffolds.

steps.title: Assemble with SPAdes
steps.instruction: Run SPAdes with its default K‑mers of 99 and 127 and retain the assembly that yields the minimal number of scaffolds.

steps.title: Assemble with Abyss
steps.instruction: Run Abyss using a K‑mer of 64 to generate an additional assembly.

steps.title: Integrate assemblies with CISA
steps.instruction: Combine the SOAPdenovo, SPAdes and Abyss assemblies using CISA software and select the integrated result that has the least scaffolds.

steps.title: Close gaps in assembly
steps.instruction: Apply GapClose software to the integrated assembly to fill remaining gaps.

steps.title: Remove low‑depth contaminant reads
steps.instruction: Filter out reads whose sequencing depth is lower than 0.35 × the average depth of coverage.

steps.title: Filter short fragments
steps.instruction: Discard assembled fragments shorter than 500 bp.

steps.title: Finalize assembly for annotation
steps.instruction: Prepare the cleaned, gap‑closed assembly for gene prediction; note that overall genome coverage exceeds 99 %.
